lines.en: Morning of October 8
Making coffee, scrolling AI news as always
when I saw Anthropic had released a new model
Claude Haiku 5.5
They said on average
it's about 75% cheaper than the last one
My first thought was great news
my bill's getting thinner
Then that same week
the same company rolled out a new feature
where one line could spin up 1,000 AI agents
all working for you at once
Even their own docs warn you
this feature burns through a ton of tokens
So what's a token
China's National Data Administration put it well
it's like data traffic in the internet era
AI reads some text, writes some text
all billed by the token
Early 2024
the tokens we used nationwide each day
were 100 billion
By this March, it hit 140 trillion
More than 1,000 times in two years
Unit price kept falling, usage kept climbing
and so did the money spent
The cheaper it got, the more we spent
Sounds off, I know
But 160 years ago
someone had already put it in a book
This is Pixel Breath
Today, let's talk about
why the cheaper AI gets, the more you spend
To be fair
thinking a price cut saves money isn't dumb at all
Veggies get cheaper, you spend less
Gas gets cheaper, a full tank costs tens less
But that math
hides an unspoken assumption
that you buy the same amount
Same veggies, same tank of gas
because that's all you ever needed
But for some things, cheaper means more
We've actually all been through this
with mobile data
Back in 2014, when 4G just arrived
Xinhua interviewed a man named Xu
to save data he turned off photo autoload on Weibo
turned off video autoplay on WeChat
and always asked for the WiFi password
I bet you've done that too
Then came speed-ups and price cuts, and by 2019
mobile data rates
had dropped over 90% from 2014
So did you save on your bill
Most people didn't
because you started scrolling short videos
In 2014 the average person used 205 MB a month
by 2024 it was 18 GB
roughly 90 times as much
A 2019 CAICT report
put it bluntly
usage grew so fast your bill barely dropped
So your bill is really just multiplication
unit price times usage
The unit price is set by the company
The usage is set by you
A price-cut headline tells half the story
Last month I took a VC class at Peking University
Liu Yong put it more plainly
you can't judge AI's cost just by the token price
but look at a done task you can sign off on
and how much it all costs
AI does 80%, a person covers the other 20%
So that labor has to count too
AI right now is just like data back then
Honestly, I'm exactly like that
my English is so-so
Last month Xiaomi put out a paper in English
so I just handed it to AI
and had it write up detailed notes
This kind of use, back when AI was pricey
hardly anyone bothered with it
So the real question is
once it's cheaper, how much will usage grow
In 1865 the British economist Jevons
wrote a book called The Coal Question
Back then Britons worried coal would run out
but many weren't worried
since steam engines would get more efficient and fix it
There was evidence for that
Watt's improved engine did the same work
and cut coal use by more than two-thirds
But Jevons said it was just the opposite
Translated, his own words were roughly this
to think saving fuel means burning less
is a total confusion, and the truth is the opposite
Basically, once steam engines saved coal
they became worth using
At first only mines put them in
then textile mills, ironworks, trains, and ships
all got one too
The coal Britain mined each year
was about 5 million tons in 1750
and over 60 million tons by 1850
more than tenfold in a century
Sure, each engine saved coal
but their numbers grew faster
Later, people called this the Jevons paradox
The more efficient, the more use climbs instead
Whether that happens comes down to one thing
once it's cheaper, how much usage jumps
Let's say
the price drops to a quarter
If usage only doubles, spending is halved
Now that's real savings
If usage quadruples, you break even exactly
If usage goes up tenfold
spending ends up at 2.5 times what it was
So which one is AI
Google's monthly token count
was 9.7 trillion two years ago
and by this May it topped 3,200 trillion
up more than 300 times in two years
The money went up too
Just Anthropic alone
saw its revenue jump 12 times last year
And it's not just more things happening
each task itself is using more too
DeepSeek has a cheap model
the new version got more accurate
but the cost per question actually rose 2.5 times
Because today's AI thinks a little longer
the longer it thinks, the more tokens it burns
Last January
when DeepSeek's cheap model came out
people worried we'd need way less computing power
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
posted a tweet in the wee hours that day
Jevons paradox strikes again
He said as AI gets more efficient and accessible
we'll see its use skyrocket
turning it into a commodity we just can't get enough of
He sells compute, so of course he'd want that
But the numbers these past two years back him up
Anthropic has a
$200 monthly plan
Last year one user
burned through tens of thousands of dollars in usage
forcing them to add weekly limits
Sima Guang once said
thrift to luxury is easy, luxury to thrift is hard
Once your usage stretches wider
it's hard to shrink it back down
So does that mean every price cut
always ends up costing you more
Not always
Salt at half price, you won't eat twice as much
The Jevons paradox only hits one kind of thing
where a little cheaper sparks new uses
Coal was like that, so was data
and now AI is too
So next time you see a price cut
don't rush to count the savings
ask one more thing
once it's cheaper, will I use more
If the answer is yes
then skip the unit price, add up the total
Set a monthly cap, stop once you hit it
For each task, add up the cost, worth it or not
Of course, spending more isn't always a bad thing
Back then, the British bought more and more coal
and got back a whole Industrial Revolution
What really matters is whether that extra spending
bought you something more
I'm planning this week
to pull up my AI bill
skip the unit price
and redo the math task by task
Back to that news from the morning of October 8
That 75%
didn't make anyone's bill thinner
It turned AI from an occasional question
into 1,000 AI agents launching at once
Here's one last question
one I'm still turning over myself
If AI keeps getting cheaper and anyone can use it
then the part it can't do but still needs a person
won't it actually get more valuable
See you next time

perChunk.judgeNotes:
Hardest calls:
1) Cues 1-8 (one long run-on sentence): built as "The morning of October 8, I was making coffee, scrolling AI news like always, when I saw Anthropic had released a new model, Claude Haiku 5.5. They said on average it's about 75% cheaper than the last one. My first thought was, great, my bill's getting thinner." Cue1 is a refrain with cue180 (not in this chunk) — kept the plain clause form "The morning of October 8" (21.8 cps on a 1.1s cue, under the 25 hard cap but above the 20 aim; the short duration makes any phrasing of this length run slightly hot).
2) Cue7/8: merged into an interjection pattern ("My first thought was, great" / "my bill's getting thinner") so "great" reads as the exclamation itself rather than describing the thought — this is a soft comma splice but matches natural spoken delivery. Chose "bill"/"thinner" wording deliberately since this is the 账单变薄 refrain (also at cue182, outside this chunk) — future cue182 should reuse exactly "bill" + "thinner".
3) Cue13/14: picked "Even their own docs warn you" + "this feature burns through a ton of tokens", dropping the relative pronoun "that" (common, natural in spoken English: "docs warn you this feature burns through tokens").
4) Cues 16-19 form one explanatory run-on (China's National Data Administration analogy → AI reads/writes → billing). Picked candidate C's shorter "AI reads some text, writes some text" over A's longer version purely to keep the cps comfortable across this dense four-cue stretch, and trimmed cue19 to "all billed by the token" (vs. the "and you're billed by the token" candidate) to stay under the 20cps aim on the short 1.73s/1.3s-class cues.
5) Cue23: none of the three candidates were capitalized for what is actually a new sentence (not a continuation of cue22's "were 100 billion"), so I merged B/C's wording with a capital: "By this March, it hit 140 trillion".
6) Verified every number against the mandatory table (75%, 1,000 AI agents, 100 billion, 140 trillion, 1,000 times, 160 years) and confirmed no line ends in punctuation and all lines stay under the 55-char hard cap and 25 cps hard cap (full per-line length/cps check run programmatically).

rejected.reason: Keeping 'that' preserves the clear grammatical link back to 'an unspoken assumption' in cue 39 (now shortened), so the two cues read as one clean sentence. Dropping it would leave a dangling reduced-relative clause that reads awkwardly. Current cps (21.8) is within the hard 25 cps ceiling, so the trim isn't necessary.

The suggested 'because now you watch short videos' drops the 开始 (started) nuance and the 刷 (scrolling/casual-swiping) flavor that the original 'because you started scrolling short videos' captures, weakening the before/after narrative. Current cps (20.3) only marginally exceeds the aim band and is well under the 25 cps hard limit, so preserving meaning takes priority over the small trim.

perChunk.judgeNotes: Hardest calls: (1) 34-35 merged into one flowing sentence ("To be fair" / lowercase "thinking a price cut saves money isn't dumb at all") rather than treating 35 as its own capitalized sentence, to read more naturally; kept "at all" despite the extra length for fidelity to 一点都不傻. (2) 47-50 restructured as one continuous sentence describing Mr Xu's data-saving habits, using parallel "turned off photo autoload on Weibo" / "turned off video autoplay on WeChat" for rhythm. (3) 52-54 kept as one sentence across three cues ("Then came speed-ups and price cuts, and by 2019 / mobile data rates / had dropped over 90% from 2014"); used "over 90%" per the explicit 九成多 mapping rather than candidates' "more than 90%". (4) 63: replaced the literal "per-person" with "your bill" to shorten (53→43 chars) while preserving the 人均 (per-capita) sense through direct address, and to echo "your bill" in cue 64. (5) 69: chose "took" over "audited" for a more natural spoken register even though Peking University pushes reading speed to ~22 cps (still under the 25 hard cap, and shorter than the "audited" alternative). (6) 74-75: rejected candidate C's conditional "If AI does 80%... so labor has to count" (awkward if/so pairing) in favor of two independent sentences. (7) 85: fixed the 便宜了以后 refrain to "once it's cheaper" for consistency with its other occurrences at cues 112 and 166 outside this chunk.

Hardest calls:
- 96-97 (Jevons quote): none of the three candidate sets matched the original wording closely enough, so I wrote a merge ("to think saving fuel means burning less" / "is a total confusion, the truth is the opposite") that splits the subject clause (96, matches Chinese 96) from the predicate (97, matches Chinese 97) and stays close to "confusion of ideas... the very contrary is the truth."
- 92-93: merged across candidates — kept "Watt's improved engine did the same work" (92) but used C's shorter "and cut coal use by more than two-thirds" for 93 instead of A's 55-char version, since it reads as one continuous sentence and is far less cramped.
- 100-102: picked wording using singular "one"/"them" to stay consistent with 102's "all got one too" rather than mixing singular/plural across the three cues.
- 107-108: merged B+C ("Sure, each engine saved coal" / "but their numbers grew even faster") for the most natural spoken concessive contrast.
- 115/117: rewrote shorter than all three candidates ("If usage only doubles, spending is halved"; "If usage quadruples, you break even exactly") to pull them back near the 42-char aim and keep the three usage-multiplier examples (double/quadruple/tenfold) parallel in structure.
- 88: swapped "the British" for "Britons" (not in any candidate) purely to cut length under the 42-char aim without changing meaning.
- 112: rewrote to front-load "once it gets cheaper" so the 便宜了以后 refrain (shared with cues 85/166 outside this chunk, confirmed via srt_cues.json) uses a reusable, consistent phrase rather than burying it mid-clause as all three candidates did.
- Capitalization: fixed two cues (110, 116) where the chosen candidate text started lowercase but is actually a new sentence, not a continuation, per the style rule.

rejected.reason: Rejected the '12x' suggestion: the numbers rule explicitly maps 12 倍 to '12 times' with no 'or 12x' alternative (unlike 90 倍 which explicitly allows 90x). Line is already under the hard 55-char max and well under 25 cps (20.21), so no change needed; kept '12 times' to satisfy the numeral style rule.

perChunk.judgeNotes:
Hardest calls:
- 121-124 (Google token stats): picked A/C "Google's monthly token count" over B's "Every month, the tokens Google processes" because B's present-tense framing clashes with "was/were...two years ago" that follows; chose C's "and by this May it topped" (123) and "up more than 300 times" (124) so the three cues read as one flowing sentence with correct tense/pronoun agreement ("it topped...up more than 300 times").
- 126-127: merged A's "Just Anthropic alone" with C's "saw its revenue jump" (rather than A's verb alone) so the pronoun "its" ties "revenue" back to "Anthropic alone" — none of the three full candidates paired the best subject with the best verb on their own.
- 130-132: reassigned sentence boundaries — treated 130 "DeepSeek has a cheap model" as a complete sentence and capitalized 131 "The new version got more accurate" as a new sentence (not a continuation of 130), then let 132 "but the cost...actually rose 2.5 times" (closest to 反而) continue it.
- 133-134: kept the literal "thinks a little longer" / "the longer it thinks, the more tokens it burns" pairing despite surface repetition — it mirrors the Chinese's cause-then-general-rule structure and reads as a natural spoken rhetorical device, not a translation error.
- 140-143 (Nadella tweet): used the real published tweet's wording where it diverges from the literal Chinese — chose B's "commodity" (143) over "something," since the task instructs staying close to known English originals even though 东西 literally means "thing."
- 146-150 (Anthropic statement): swapped in A's "burned through tens of thousands of dollars in usage" for 149 instead of my first instinct (C), because "in usage" mirrors the real Anthropic phrasing "model usage" better while B/C options drop that nuance; capitalized 148 "Last year one user" as a fresh sentence rather than using the given "and last year" since the plan description in 146-147 is a complete clause.
- 152 (Sima Guang): chose the shorter A/B wording "thrift to luxury is easy, luxury to thrift is hard" (50 chars) over C's "going from...going back" (55 chars, at the hard cap) for safer reading speed, lowercased to continue "Sima Guang once said."

rejected.reason: Rejected the suggested 'Back to that October 8 morning news' — it reorders the refrain phrase 10月8号早上 into an 'October 8 morning' noun-compound, which breaks consistency with cue 1's standalone rendering of the same Chinese phrase (likely 'the morning of October 8'). The original is only marginally over the soft 20cps aim (20.2 cps) and well under the 25cps hard max, so it's not worth risking the refrain match for a 0.2cps trim. Kept unchanged.

perChunk.judgeNotes: Hardest calls: (1) 159-160: merged/trimmed to "The Jevons paradox only hits one kind of thing" + "where a little cheaper sparks new uses" so the two read as one relative clause and reading speed drops from ~20.6 to ~18.6 cps. (2) 166: kept Chinese clause order ("once it's cheaper, will I use more") rather than inverting, on the assumption this matches how the 便宜了以后 refrain was likely rendered at cues 85/112 elsewhere in the episode — could not verify those cues' actual text since they're outside this chunk. (3) 183-184: chose "It turned AI from an occasional question" / "into firing up 1,000 AI agents at once" to explicitly echo cue 11's "1,000 AI agents" wording (per the numbers rule and the stated 184↔11 refrain), accepting a slightly loose noun/gerund parallelism ("question" vs "firing up...") since the Chinese original has the same looseness. (4) 180: kept "the morning of October 8" (not "October 8 morning") to preserve the 10月8号早上 refrain in natural English, even though it pushes reading speed to ~20.2 cps (still under the 25 hard cap). (5) 161: rendered 流量 as "mobile data" rather than bare "data," based on chapter 2 context (cues 17/45/53 in the full script all frame 流量 as mobile data usage). (6) 174-175: reordered into "What really matters is whether that extra spending" / "bought you something more" so the two cues form one clean conditional clause rather than the clunkier "...the extra you spent and whether it bought..." options. (7) 164: switched to "don't rush to count the savings" over "calculate" for a better reading-speed margin with no meaning loss. All 36 lines stay within the hard 55-char / 25-cps caps; several (158,159,161,170,171,172,174,180,187,188) exceed the 42-char soft aim but were kept because shortening further would cut required content (refrains, numbers, proper nouns) or break the cross-cue sentence flow.

finalIssues.problem: Chinese 三百多倍 should map to "more than 300 times" per the style guide (and matches the established pattern used elsewhere for similar multiples: cue 24 "More than 1,000 times", cue 106 "more than tenfold"). The current line uses "over 300 times" instead, breaking that consistency.

"My first thought was great" reads ambiguously on first pass — it can parse as "the thought itself was a great one" rather than "my reaction was: great." A small reword removes the hiccup while keeping the meaning and the lowercase continuation into cue 8 ("my bill's getting thinner") intact.

The cue break leaves "Anthropic has a" dangling on the bare article "a," which reads awkwardly as a standalone on-screen line even though it's grammatical once cue 147 follows. Rephrasing avoids ending the line on an unsupported article.

Fixing the awkward bare-article ending would require also editing cue 147, which is out of scope here, so the original is kept to preserve grammatical continuity across the two cues.
